title: fix(2d): peck a contour dive deeper than one stepdown below the cut floor
body:
## What changed

A contour dive below its ring's first level pecks when it would cut more than one stepdown below the cleared floor. This applies to dives past tabs and wall-side graze dives, including tabbed bore entries.

Each peck feeds one stepdown, retracts above the material, and returns above the last depth before the next feed. One note describes the pecked entry. The uncut floor is the material top, or one stepdown above a lower ring's first level. The first level never pecks.

The floor check now proves coverage of the entire tool disc. An exact matching endpoint or plunge column proves coverage. An axis-aligned straight feed also proves coverage when the target centre lies on its centreline. Uncertain coverage counts as uncut material. The proof does not use finite samples or approximate arc chords.

The old 4,096-peck cap no longer permits a long final cut. Every required stepdown is retained within the existing contour depth limit.

The XY path, tab layout, leads, and level order stay the same.

## Cause

The levels above cut the lead-in start of a tab window only at the ring start. Other windows can start above a 2.5 mm crescent of uncut material. The original dive cut 18 mm below that floor. The stay-down ramp preset cut 13.5 mm at window 0.

The review also found an uncovered rim with a 0.002 mm perpendicular lead. The shortened sample radius missed it. The peck cap could append a 9.04 mm final cut for a 0.01 mm stepdown.

## Pins and mutation proof

The L-shape fixture is in `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_entry.rs`. Its independent oracle now samples the actual tool radius and counts straight plunge columns. It measures circular sweeps analytically. Inscribed chords create artificial gaps at the full rim, so they no longer stand in for earlier flat arcs. The safety assertions stay the same.

- `no_contour_descent_goes_more_than_one_stepdown_below_the_disc_floor` checks all descents of four entry presets.
- `a_short_perpendicular_lead_pecks_below_the_uncut_rim` checks the public generator with a 0.002 mm lead and a 0.0001 mm tolerance.
- `an_offset_column_leaves_an_uncut_rim` checks a prior column that misses the actual rim.
- `an_offset_straight_cut_does_not_prove_full_disc_coverage` checks an offset straight sweep and a proven centreline case.
- `a_dive_beyond_4096_pecks_preserves_every_stepdown` checks all 5,000 depths down to Z-50 at a 0.01 mm stepdown.
- `first_router_part_posts_the_shipped_program` checks the shipped router NC file through the CLI. Before regeneration, `first_part_programs` had one pass and one failure: the router NC pin was red.

The window readings use `(depth below floor, crescent)`. Plunge windows 1 to 3 change from `(18.0, 2.5)` to `(4.5, 2.5)`. The stay-down window 0 changes from `(13.5, 2.5)` to `(4.5, 2.5)`. Lead None remains `(2.7, 0.0)`.

Mutation proof:

- Restoring the old sampler makes `an_offset_column_leaves_an_uncut_rim` and `an_offset_straight_cut_does_not_prove_full_disc_coverage` fail. The public pin `a_short_perpendicular_lead_pecks_below_the_uncut_rim` also fails: at `(10.152613, -3.002)`, the floor is Z0 and the dive reaches Z-18. Restoring the fix passes all five peck unit tests and all five public contour tests.
- Restoring the old cap makes `a_dive_beyond_4096_pecks_preserves_every_stepdown` fail: it returns 4,097 depths instead of 5,000. Restoring the fix passes that pin.
- Restoring the literal router NC file from reviewed head `3d1564e10` makes `first_router_part_posts_the_shipped_program` fail. Restoring the final NC file passes that exact pin. The restored file matches its saved byte hash. Both `first_part_programs` tests also pass.

The final gates below cover the refreshed head. After the fixture corrections, restoring the old sampled coverage also makes `machining2d::tabs_hold_the_part_until_the_floor` fail: zero pecks instead of four. Restoring the fix passes that pin.

## Final validation

Final head: `250592fb756370115d7472412d6fe5a2c1de07d5`. Tested base: `6d0381f1977b267885e22b3ddf55950b098fd319`, fetched before the final gates. The worktree is clean. Upstream advanced after the gates started. A read-only `git merge-tree` check confirms that the final head merges cleanly with latest upstream `1e182f2cf8b55995965d2b19e99b2647afddcde4`. This check required no hand resolution. The gates do not include those newer upstream commits.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on `03d84130a9a139914e40e1a6ec8a5114d29ecc83`: 173 steps; 171 passed, 2 failed, 0 stalled, in 64.6 minutes. The two failures identified stale expectations below. On the final head, `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --failed gate-logs/quick-20261124-121421` passes both corrected steps: 2 passed, 0 failed, 0 stalled (`machining2d` and `first_router_part`).
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: RED: 104 actual steps; 103 passed, one failed, zero stalled, in 84.0 minutes. The release build passed in 1,312 seconds. The plan listed 103 steps; an existing probe expanded it to 104. Seven lanes are outside the diff reach. The failure is `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`, test `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`. At `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:79`, the mesh has 5,232 triangles; the pin expects 6,228. It fails before path generation. This mesh pin is outside the latest review findings and was not changed. Read-only diffs against tested base `6d0381f1977b267885e22b3ddf55950b098fd319` are empty for the test, STEP fixture, import chain, STEP meshing code, manifests, and lock file. These checks establish unchanged inputs; they do not reproduce the failure on the baseline. No baseline reproduction was run. The full heavy gate is red.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed on the final head in 5 minutes 16 seconds.
- `app suites: example_catalog` in the full quick gate: 41 passed, 4 ignored, in 44.81 seconds. A final-head run during the release build hit the 60-second limits for two 3D rough-finish cases. The isolated final-head retry passed all 41 tests, with four ignored, in 107.94 seconds. The rough-finish rebuild took 29.764 seconds; regeneration took 29.558 seconds.
- Final-head small suites: 49 passed. Counts: `example_catalog_adaptive` 1, `example_catalog_edge_work` 1, `first_part_programs` 2, `first_router_part` 4, `golden_cl` 34, and `solid_law_goldens` 7. Command: `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -j 2 -p camcraft-app --no-fail-fast --test example_catalog_adaptive --test example_catalog_edge_work --test first_router_part --test first_part_programs --test golden_cl --test solid_law_goldens -- --test-threads=1`.
- Router suites: `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test first_router_part --test first_part_programs -- --test-threads=1` passes all six tests. This ran before the final commit on identical source and fixture contents.
- Final-head motion pins: all five peck unit tests and all five `contour_tab_entry` tests passed. Commands: `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -j 2 -p camcraft-motion --lib contour_peck::tests:: -- --test-threads=1` and `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -j 2 -p camcraft-motion --test contour_tab_entry -- --test-threads=1`.
- Merged tested base `6d0381f1977b267885e22b3ddf55950b098fd319` after #3833 merged during this fix round. The only hand-resolved conflict was the import of `contour_peck` and `wall_ramp`. Both imports remain. No logic conflicted, and both safety guards remain.

## Goldens moved

The program changes add pecked tab-window dives. Each program was regenerated with the repository tool. The full quick gate found two stale expectations:

- `machining2d::tabs_hold_the_part_until_the_floor` counted intermediate pecks as entries. The correction keeps six entries and counts four bottom dives and four pecks separately.
- `first_router_part` found a stale cached project. Conservative coverage adds two pecks, at Z-4 and Z-8, before the first bottom-window dive at `(176, 80.991)`.

- `examples/catalog/2d/contour-tabs/contour-tabs.nc`: generated with `cargo xtask catalog --case 2d/contour-tabs`. Three dives now feed through Z4, Z2, and Z0, with retracts between pecks. The original change adds 18 lines. This fix round makes no further change to this golden.
- `examples/catalog/2d/contour-tabs/contour-tabs.camproj`: the cached path contains the same moves. The project save updates its version from 77 to 78.
- `examples/first-router-part.camproj`: generated with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1` and `first_router_part`. The tab-window dives now peck through Z-4, Z-8, and Z-12. The note is added. Final regeneration also updates the initial bottom window at `(176, 80.991)`. The exact regeneration hook, `WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-app --test first_router_part first_router_part_project_loads_verifies_and_posts_to_grblhal -- --exact --test-threads=1`, passes. The project correction adds 82 lines and removes one relative to the first refreshed head.
- `examples/first-router-part.nc`: regenerated with `cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- process examples/first-router-part.camproj -o examples/first-router-part.nc` (exit 0). Three direct dives now peck through Z-4, Z-8, and Z-12. The initial regeneration added 18 lines. Regeneration of the updated cached project adds the first bottom-window pecks as well. The final diff adds 24 lines relative to the reviewed head `3d1564e10`: 18 for the three later windows and six for the initial bottom window at `(176, 80.991)`.

`contour_tabs_case_posts_the_lead_moves_and_the_tab_lifts` counts peck retracts separately from lead-out lifts: six of each. The case README states this distinction.

## Not exercised

Windows and macOS were not built. The light tier was not run separately. The heavy gate excludes seven lanes that the diff does not reach. This PR changes no UI; screenshots do not apply.

The lead-in arc after a tab window still feeds through the 2.5 mm crescent at the target level. This issue addresses the plunge only.

## Overlaps and decision

- #3834 also touches `contour.rs`, `contour_step.rs`, and the `Step` constructor. The second PR to merge needs a refresh.
- #3833 is incorporated through the merge of the tested base.

`docs/decisions/3678-tab-window-dive.md` records the peck, conservative coverage proof, and removal of the unsafe peck cap. Cutting the window lead-ins on earlier levels was dropped because it changes the XY travel.

Effort: high

Changelog: 2D Contour: a dive past a tab (and the stay-down entry of a tabbed level) that goes more than one stepdown below the floor the levels above cut now pecks one stepdown at a time, with a note.

Fixes #3678
